extracted.intended_audience: IP policymakers, researchers, statisticians and national IP office staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and notes for interpreting the WIPO World Intellectual Property Indicators trademark tables and charts (definitions, selection rules, coverage, and methodological caveats). Intended to help read and compare trademark statistics across offices and origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry sector classification (Edital / Nice classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry sectors based on class groups are those defined by Edital. Some industry sectors are abbreviated. See annex B for full definitions and the composition of Nice goods and services classes. See www.wipo.int/en/web/classification-nice for a complete list of classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures using 'industry sectors' map Nice classification classes into sector groups as defined by Edital; consult annex B and the Nice classification link for exact class-to-sector mappings. Be aware some sectors are abbreviated in charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of resident vs non-resident filing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures are based on non-resident filing data from 141 IP offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many charts explicitly report whether counts are resident, non-resident or total; ensure you use the right category when comparing across offices or origins (e.g., industry-sector charts may use non-resident application class counts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source and coverage for world totals
rubrics_metrics.description: Source: WIPO Statistics Database, September 2025. World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering 155 IP offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the source note and number of offices covered for each figure—world totals may be estimates and office coverage can differ by figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark registrations in force definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Data refer to the number of trademark registrations in force, not the number of classes specified in those registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Registrations in force’ counts active registrations (a registration can include multiple classes). Do not conflate registrations-in-force counts with application or registration class counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark life-cycle and renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark rights can be maintained indefinitely by paying a renewal fee at defined intervals. Trademarks in force provides information on the volume of trademark registrations currently active, as well as the historical trademark life cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret trends in registrations-in-force in light of renewal rules and the potential for indefinite maintenance; growth/decline may reflect renewal behaviour as well as new registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonization caveat across offices
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO collects data from IP offices using a common questionnaire and methodology. However, due to differences in application processing procedures between offices, data cannot be fully harmonized. Therefore, caution should be exercised when making comparisons across offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons across offices may be affected by procedural and reporting differences; use caution and consult office-specific notes where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection rule: top three sectors / top offices/origins
rubrics_metrics.description: The top three sectors and top offices were selected based on 2024 totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reading charts that show 'top three sectors' or 'top offices', understand selection is by 2024 totals—smaller offices or sectors may be excluded by design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for 'selected 20 origins' (GDP-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: The selected 20 origins for 2024 were included if they had a GDP greater than USD 535 billion PPP and a resident trademark application class count of at least 25,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charts using this selection show a subset built to compare large-economy origins; they are not an overall ranking of all origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for 'selected 20 origins' (population-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: The selected 20 origins for 2024 were included if they had a population greater than 2.5 million and a resident trademark application class count of at least 3,500.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Population-filtered selections are intended to compare origins above a minimum population and activity threshold; interpret as a curated sample rather than a full ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: GDP data reference year and unit
rubrics_metrics.description: GDP data are in 2021 US purchasing power parity (PPP) dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relating trademark counts to GDP use the stated PPP baseline year (2021) to ensure consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of percentages for registrations-in-force by registration year
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages are calculated as follows: the number of trademark registrations issued in year t and in force in 2024 divided by the total number of trademark registrations issued in year t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formula measures the share of registrations from a given year that remained active in 2024; coverage for this indicator depends on offices that provided breakdowns by year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage limitation for year-breakdown indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: This figure is based on about 23.8 million active trademark registrations reported by the 86 offices that provided a breakdown by year of registration. Detailed data for several of the larger offices, such as those of Argentina, China and Japan, are unavailable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret percentage-of-registrations-in-force statistics knowing they omit some large offices and therefore do not represent all registrations worldwide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote data caveats and special cases (a–h)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Data on application class count by origin are incomplete, because some offices do not report detailed statistics containing the origin of application class counts. (b) Only Madrid designation data are available therefore application class count by office and origin data are incomplete. (c) This country does not have a national trademark office. All applications for trademark protection are filed at the Benelux Office for Intellectual Property or the European Union Intellectual Property Office. (d) Resident applications include those filed by residents of Belgium, Luxembourg and the Kingdom of the Netherlands. (e) Resident applications include those filed by residents of EU member states. (f) Total includes an aggregate direct application class count that cannot be broken down into direct and non-resident components. (g) The African Intellectual Property Office (OAPI) is the competent office for processing applications. (h) This country or municipality is not a Madrid member. The Kingdom of the Netherlands has extended the application of the Madrid Protocol to the territories of Curaçao and Sint Maarten, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the lettered footnotes to understand special reporting arrangements and incompleteness. Many table cells are impacted by these special cases—do not assume uniform reporting across all entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation legend
rubrics_metrics.description: n.a. indicates not applicable. .. indicates not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the notation legend to distinguish true zeros from missing or inapplicable data when reading tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acronym clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: EUIPO is the European Union Intellectual Property Office. Iran is the Islamic Republic of Iran. ARIPO is the African Regional Intellectual Property Organization. BOIP is the Benelux Office for Intellectual Property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be attentive to office and country name variants and acronyms used in tables and charts to avoid misattributing data.
